easy.explanation: He cries to the LORD, whom he calls the God of his salvation.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist cry?

easy.explanation: He says that he has cried before the LORD both day and night.
easy.q: When does the psalmist cry before the LORD?

easy.explanation: He asks, “Let my prayer come before thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do with his prayer?

answers: As the God of his salvation
As the king of the dead
As one who has abandoned him
medium.explanation: He addresses the LORD as “O LORD God of my salvation.”
medium.q: How does the psalmist describe the LORD at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Crying, prayer, and a request to be heard
medium.explanation: He cries to God, asks that his prayer come before Him, and asks Him to incline His ear.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the psalmist’s words?

medium.explanation: The phrase is a request for the LORD to listen attentively to the psalmist’s cry.
medium.q: What does “incline thine ear” mean in this passage?

answers: The crying continues throughout the whole day
The psalmist stops praying at night
The prayer occurs only at one particular time
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both day and night emphasizes the continual nature of his cry.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the movement from “day” to “night”?

answers: The psalmist wants to move away from God
He asks both that his prayer reach God and that God listen to it
He announces that his prayer has already been answered
challenge.explanation: The two requests express his desire for his prayer to reach God and be heard by Him.
challenge.q: What is the connection between “Let my prayer come before thee” and “incline thine ear”?

answers: The tension between singing and silence
The tension between day and night only
The tension between constant crying and the need to be heard
challenge.explanation: The psalmist continually cries to the LORD and asks Him to listen.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in the opening verses?

easy.explanation: He says, “For my soul is full of troubles.”
easy.q: What is the psalmist’s soul full of?

answers: As the strength of a king
easy.explanation: He says that he is like a man who has no strength.
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe his strength?

answers: In the lowest pit, in darkness, and in the deeps
easy.explanation: He says, “Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, in darkness, in the deeps.”
easy.q: Where does the psalmist say he has been laid?

answers: His troubles make him feel that his life is near the grave
He says there is no connection
medium.explanation: After saying that his soul is full of troubles, he says that his life draws near to the grave.
medium.q: What connection does the psalmist make between his troubles and his life?

medium.explanation: “The deeps” refers to profound depths and emphasizes the darkness of his condition.
medium.q: What does “the deeps” mean in this passage?

answers: The LORD put his acquaintances far from him and made him an abomination to them
medium.explanation: The psalmist says that the LORD put his acquaintances far from him and made him an abomination to them.
medium.q: What caused the psalmist’s isolation according to these verses?

challenge.explanation: The image presents a person without the power to act or escape.
challenge.q: Which image most strongly expresses the psalmist’s helplessness?

answers: From troubles and death toward the pit, darkness, and separation from acquaintances
challenge.explanation: The verses move from inward trouble to images of death, darkness, confinement, and social isolation.
challenge.q: How do the descriptions of distress build throughout the passage?

answers: The psalmist is about to leave immediately
The psalmist is attending a celebration
The psalmist feels unable to escape his condition
challenge.explanation: Being shut up and unable to come forth expresses a feeling of having no way out.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the statement “I am shut up, and I cannot come forth”?

paragraphs.title: Prayer Without an Answer and Questions About the Dead

answers: He turns away from the LORD
easy.explanation: He says, “LORD, I have called daily upon thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist do daily?

answers: He stretches them out to the LORD
He puts them in his pockets
easy.explanation: He says, “I have stretched out my hands unto thee.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist do with his hands?

easy.explanation: He says, “In the morning shall my prayer prevent thee.”
easy.q: When does the psalmist say his prayer will come before the LORD?

answers: God’s lovingkindness, faithfulness, wonders, and righteousness
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks about lovingkindness, faithfulness, wonders, and righteousness.
medium.q: Which things does the psalmist ask whether they can be shown or declared among the dead?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the realm of the dead as a place of forgetfulness.
medium.q: What does “the land of forgetfulness” mean in this passage?

answers: Because he stops speaking to the LORD
Because he wants to praise himself
Because he wonders whether God’s works are known in the realm of the dead
medium.explanation: His questions ask whether God’s lovingkindness, faithfulness, wonders, and righteousness can be known there.
medium.q: Why are the psalmist’s questions about the dead connected to his prayer?

answers: He continues turning to God despite feeling unanswered
challenge.explanation: Even in distress and uncertainty, he still brings his prayer before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the prayer coming before the LORD in the morning reveal about the psalmist?

answers: Continual prayer contrasted with a felt lack of response
challenge.explanation: The psalmist calls and stretches out his hands, while the passage records his unanswered questions rather than a response.
challenge.q: What contrast is especially clear in this passage?

answers: To express doubt about whether God’s goodness and righteousness are known in the realm of the dead
To announce that the dead have answered him
To describe the happiness of the dead
challenge.explanation: The questions examine whether God’s lovingkindness, faithfulness, wonders, and righteousness are revealed there.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the many questions about the dead?

paragraphs.title: Surrounded by Suffering and Abandoned by Loved Ones

answers: Why He casts off his soul and hides His face
easy.explanation: He asks, “LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD?

easy.explanation: He says, “I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up.”
easy.q: Since when does the psalmist describe himself as afflicted?

easy.explanation: He says, “Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, and mine acquaintance into darkness.”
easy.q: Who has been put far from the psalmist at the end of the passage?

answers: They come around him daily like water
They pass like a light breeze
medium.explanation: He says, “They came round about me daily like water; they compassed me about together.”
medium.q: How does the psalmist describe the way his troubles surround him?

answers: God’s terrors have overwhelmed and disordered him
He rejoices because of God’s fears
medium.explanation: The statement portrays him as overwhelmed and mentally distressed by the LORD’s terrors.
medium.q: What does the phrase “I suffer thy terrors I am distracted” communicate?

answers: Both express a sense of abandonment and loneliness
medium.explanation: The hidden face of the LORD and the removal of loved ones both deepen the psalmist’s isolation.
medium.q: What connection exists between the LORD hiding His face and the distance of the psalmist’s loved ones?

answers: The distress surrounds him from every side and continues daily
The psalmist is in a peaceful place
challenge.explanation: The surrounding waters represent continuing pressure with no room for escape.
challenge.q: What does the image “They came round about me daily like water” emphasize?

answers: From the psalmist’s question to the LORD to the separation of his loved ones and acquaintances
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with a question about God’s rejection and ends with the psalmist isolated from those close to him.
challenge.q: How does the passage develop from its first statement to its last?

answers: It has continued from his youth
challenge.explanation: He explicitly says that he has been afflicted and ready to die “from my youth up.”
challenge.q: What detail about the duration of the psalmist’s suffering is easy to overlook?
